Tigers don't usually eat their prey at the kill site - but instead drag their prey into cover to feed. If a tiger leaves - say to get a drink - it will cover it's kill by raking leaves, dirt, grass and even rocks over the carcass. 3. Tigers primarily hunt deer, but as opportunistic predators, they can also eat wild boars, birds, fish, rodents, amphibians, reptiles, and even insects. Be Human Like a Tiger A tiger doesn't roar to prove strength. It moves in silence. It waits, watches, and chooses its moment. Not every battle is worth energy. A tiger walks alone-not because it's lonely, but because it trusts itself. Scars don't make it weaker; they remind it that it survived. When a tiger strikes, it commits fully. No hesitation. No doubt. It doesn't chase approval. The jungle already knows what it is. Life lesson: Move with purpose. Speak less, observe more. Protect your energy. Trust your power.
